correctness.rationale: For each n, W^n has explicit orthogonal residue rays of norm one. Norm attainment on each ray forces an all-unit length-n window; conversely one such window per ray gives a cyclic spanning family from the norm-one eigenspace E of (W^n)*W^n. A nonzero reducing-subspace projection commuting with W^n and its adjoint must meet E, proving universal attaining restrictions. If L=m-d+1>=d-g+1 then the complement of F_s in Z/d has <=g-1 elements, leaving an intact residue class mod g and forcing every target d-residue. If L<=d-g, complementary g consecutive residues permit CRT placement of m-window starts avoiding a target d-residue; m<d is immediate by isolated blocks. Compactness and norm closeness follow from the explicit null perturbations. The modulus conclusion follows exactly from infinitely many diagonal entries below the limiting supremum versus finitely many exceptional entries. The external checker passed 900 arithmetic tests and all small CRT witnesses; the infinite assertions rest on the displayed proof.

value.rationale: The problem of stability of norm-attainment on every reducing subspace is explicitly central to Su--Zhang 2026. A sharp, all-pairs arithmetic forcing threshold is a natural complete power-stability invariant, with surprising nonmonotone behavior (m=4 fails to force d=3). The CRT construction shows every sharp failure already near the shift in the compact-perturbation norm, and the beta/beta0 distinction persists simultaneously for all powers. These are structural, not isolated numerical, results with direct applications to recognizing power-stability and separation of norm-attainment classes.
